Endocrinologist

City Hospital

Suit 32, 55 Main Road                                                                                          Comment [Benchmark1]: Suite

Newtown

24/01/2015

Dear Dr Cross,

Re: Mr Brett Collister, 45 years of age                                                                        Comment [Benchmark2]: DOB: 20
                                                                                                               November 1970
I am writing to refer Mr Collister, a 45-year-old factory foreman, whose features are suggestive of diabetes
mellitus . Your assessment would be highly appreciated.                                                        Comment [Benchmark3]: type 2

Mr Collister is married with three children. Unfortunately, he is overweight.                                  Comment [Benchmark4]: ; however,
                                                                                                               he has no known allergies.
On 22/03/2014, the patient initially came suffering from upper respiratory tract infection, for which he was   Comment [Benchmark5]: an
given a supportive treatment. A week later, he suffered from acute tonsillitis. Thus, amoxicillin was          Comment [Benchmark6]: and thus
prescribed. On 17/08/2014, the patient presented with left shoulder pain. Consequently, he was given
ibuprofen and was referred to physiotherapist. On 26/10/2014, the patient experienced right knee pain          Comment [Benchmark7]: a
mostly due to osteoarthritis. As a result, he was instructed to take ibuprofen and to decrease weight. On
4/01/2015, regrettably, he did not modify his sedentary lifestyle. Moreover, he reported pain in both eyes
together with dizziness. Thus, some blood tests were requested.

Today, in addition to the previous visit’s complaints, the patient experienced visual disturbances.
Unfortunately, the test results revealed high random and fasting blood glucose levels besides an increase
in HDL/LDL.

In light of the above, the patient is being referred for further management. Should you have any queries,
please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
